chain.label: Maintenance personnel called in on off-duty days to earlier-than-normal shifts
chain.trigger: the mechanic and the inspector were contacted to report to work on an off-duty day (December 6)...work shift began about 6 hours earlier than his regularly scheduled shift

chain.label: Mechanic and QC inspector fatigued during the December 6 maintenance shift
chain.trigger: both the mechanic's performance and the inspector's performance probably were degraded by fatigue

caused_by.evidence: because both the mechanic and the inspector had insufficient time to adjust to working an earlier shift than normal, they were experiencing fatigue during the December 6 shift

chain.label: Maintenance documentation lacked work cards with delineated, individually-verified steps
chain.trigger: the maintenance documentation did not clearly delineate specific inspection steps, which can allow these tasks to be more vulnerable to error through human factors

chain.label: Mechanic reused a degraded self-locking nut and improperly installed or omitted the split pin on the fore/aft servo input rod connection
chain.trigger: the hardware was improperly secured during maintenance that had been conducted the day before the accident

caused_by.evidence: contributed to the improper securing of the fore/aft servo connection hardware
the maintenance documentation did not clearly delineate specific inspection steps

chain.label: Fore/aft servo input rod secured only by a degraded nut with no functioning split pin backup
chain.trigger: no backup mechanism for a self-locking nut with degraded locking ability was in place to secure the input rod to the fore/aft servo

caused_by.evidence: the fore/aft servo bolt most likely disengaged because the split pin was installed improperly or it was not installed and a self-locking nut that was either degraded or not torqued was used

chain.label: QC inspector's postmaintenance inspection failed to detect the improperly secured/missing split pin
chain.trigger: the inadequate postmaintenance inspection of the accident helicopter

caused_by.evidence: contributed to...the inadequate postmaintenance inspection of the accident helicopter
lack of clearly delineated inspection steps to follow

chain.label: In-flight vibratory loosening caused the nut to unthread, the bolt to disengage, and the servo input rod to separate from the linkage
chain.trigger: the nut became loose (likely because it was degraded) and, without the split pin, the nut separated from the bolt, the bolt disconnected, and the input rod separated from the linkage while the helicopter was in flight

caused_by.evidence: the nut became loose (likely because it was degraded) and, without the split pin, the nut separated from the bolt

the mechanic, inspector, and check pilot each had at least one opportunity to observe the fore/aft servo self-locking nut and split pin; however, they did not note that the split pin was installed improperly or not present

chain.label: Loss of the fore/aft servo input rendered the helicopter uncontrollable
chain.trigger: at which point the helicopter became uncontrollable and crashed

chain.label: Helicopter descended at a high rate and impacted mountainous terrain
chain.trigger: descended at a rate of at least 2,500 feet per minute to impact

caused_by.evidence: entered a left turn, and descended at a rate of at least 2,500 feet per minute to impact

chain.label: Pilot and four passengers killed
chain.trigger: The pilot and four passengers were killed

caused_by.evidence: The pilot and four passengers were killed, and the helicopter was destroyed by impact forces and postimpact fire
